hypothesis: Y029/Y030 suggest recency is insufficient to avoid memory-induced churn in fast drift. Current graph conflict degree may distinguish cheap-to-honor cached assignments from cached assignments that force rematching of neighboring motifs.
freeze: Predefine four memory policies, fixed conflict limits 1/2, four geometric schedules, fresh seeds and success criteria before first use; no postresult parameter selection.
population: Same Y029 exact 16 motif identities/cells, seven simultaneously active, maximum nine inactive cache entries, circular radius-two matching, eight episodes, four-way collision.
policies: matched_sham: same cache writes but no read
full: all legal prior observed assignments
conflict1: cached cell is legal and belongs to <=1 current active key neighborhood
conflict2: cached cell is legal and belongs to <=2 current active key neighborhoods
metric: Per-regime/policy heldout returning-key churn, current-graph allowed preference counts, search calls, write parity, matching cardinality. Compare conflict2 relative to full and sham.
classification: CONFLICT_FILTERED_GAIN if conflict2 strictly reduces churn relative full in BOTH drift5 and alternating and preserves at least 70% of full-cache saving under drift1; TRADEOFF if conflict2 strictly reduces churn in at least one of drift5/alternating but strict condition fails; NO_CONFLICT_GATE_GAIN otherwise. Publish all negative arms.
controls: Only present neighbor graph and previously observed stored cells accessible; no future or evaluator cumulative history
Same exact bounded cache capacity, keys/writes/occupancy
Exhaustive Hall maximum matching 7/7 each episode
Freeze source Git blobs, original first-use artifact and one full regression
claim_limit: Finite synthetic assignment preference gating; no learned semantics or production authority.
